Date Reported: [redacted date]

TEST PERFORMED
G-banded Chromosome Analysis (Karyotype)

CLINICAL INDICATION
Post rapid PCR screening for Down syndrome

METHODOLOGY
Peripheral blood lymphocytes were cultured and harvested according to standard protocols. Metaphase chromosomes were G-banded using trypsin-Giemsa technique. Analysis performed at 400-450 band resolution, sufficient for detection of numerical abnormalities and major structural rearrangements.

RESULT
Karyotype: 46,XX

No evidence of trisomy 21 detected.
No other numerical or major structural chromosomal abnormalities identified.

15 metaphase cells analyzed.

INTERPRETATION
Normal female karyotype. This result excludes Down syndrome (trisomy 21) and other major chromosomal abnormalities detectable at this resolution. The analysis complements the previous rapid PCR screening performed.

LIMITATIONS
This analysis is designed to detect numerical abnormalities and major structural rearrangements. Subtle structural abnormalities, low-level mosaicism (<20%), and submicroscopic deletions/duplications are beyond the resolution of this test.

Authorized by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Date: [redacted date]
